Nate, saw Rinsed extended the CRM into retail wash customers and folded in Ignite Wash.

Expanding into a new segment usually opens more in-market operators than the team can cover before they cool, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Rinsed off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Nate, quick follow-up for Rinsed.

As the retail segment opens up, the pipeline target climbs faster than reps can ramp. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Rinsed needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.

Nate, last bit of proof for Rinsed.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Rinsed's reply rate likely compares to other vertical-SaaS startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a vertical-SaaS motion? I will tailor it to Rinsed either way.
